text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen says that it would be for the best if a current court hearing on the legality of Denmark's EU treaties were over before any referendum on the outcome of the EU's intergovernmental conference.
--High street banks are dropping their resistance to the popular Dankort debit card as a means of payment for internet purchases. They now say that if traders cover bank costs the card may be used.

--Government plans to reduce an owner-occupier levy on householders would benefit about 0.8 percent of Danes. Thirty thousand homeowners would escape the tax altogther and 10 percent would pay a reduced rate.

--East Asiatic Company boss Michael Fiorini says that domestic public opinion is irrelevant as long as EAC's sales are abroad. "We can allow ourselves to do the business we believe is right," he said. The company is under criticism for producing weedkiller banned at home in a Thai joint-venture and selling it to the military regime in Burma.

--Danish businessman Kurt Thomsen, financed by London-based Finn Simonsen, is to seek to buy Copenhagen-listed Cederholm and Voss International for 500 million crowns. Thomsen is to place a Spanish construction project into the company if the purchase goes through.
